Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re moving toward a Reserved Capacity (dedicated) evaluation at Astrala and want to give you a realistic traffic sample so your sizing exercise isn’t overly conservative. Attached is a small telemetry extract (astrala_telemetry_sample.csv) showing 7 days of production calls.

A few things to flag up front:
- Two main product paths: "API inference" (customer-facing chat, latency sensitive) and "batch-annotate" (daily bulk runs). API makes up ~70% of tokens but is bursty.
- We see short bursts tied to marketing promos (3–10 min peaks) and predictable morning/daypart spikes.
- Average prompt length ~ 60 tokens; average response 180 tokens; 99th percentile response ~ 800 tokens.
- Session affinity: yes for chat (we pin KV cache per session for ~25 minutes).

Can you confirm the best breakdown of details you need? We can fill a short questionnaire or hop on a 30-min call — whichever is easiest. Also copying Procurement, who will need SLA/commitment language later.

Thanks,
Luke
Head of Product
Astrala AI

Hi Luke — thanks for the sample and the upfront context.

This is great. To size accurately we prefer a short, focused questionnaire that captures: steady-state QPS, burst QPS and duration, expected concurrency per session, token distribution (prompt/response percentiles), session stickiness, acceptable p99 latency, and tolerance for fallback/soft-failures. I’ve attached our one-page "traffic regimes" questionnaire (redwood_pre-sales_regimes_qs.pdf) — can you complete the fields highlighted in yellow and return?

A few quick clarifying questions from my side:
1) For the burst events, are the bursts per-route or global across routes?
2) When you say session affinity is ~25 minutes, is that an inactivity window or a maximum session lifespan?
3) Do you have a defined SLO for p99 generation latency today? If so, what is it and is it business-critical?

Marissa and Karthik are on the thread — Marissa will run the initial GPU-mix hypothesis and Karthik will review the quantization/compatibility constraints. If you prefer a 30-min sizing call we can propose slots tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Sofia / team — attached are the answers filled inline in your questionnaire and a short note on traffic topology. Key points:
- Burst shape: global fan-out triggered by marketing (approx 120–150 QPS baseline on API; bursts to 1,800 QPS for 6–9 minutes; smaller local peaks ~400 QPS).
- Session affinity: we treat sessions as active while there is less than 25 minutes of inactivity; max lifespan effectively unlimited but rare >2 hours.
- SLO: target p99 generation latency 450 ms; p50 ~ 85 ms. p99 is business-critical for the chat UX.
- Token mix: median prompt 58; median response 172; p95 response ~560; p99 ~820.
- Batch runs: consume ~20% of tokens; jobs are run in night windows and tolerate higher latency.

Attachment: completed_redwood_qs_answers.pdf (PDF, 30 KB) — I also re-attached the small telemetry extract for reference.

Luke

Thanks Luke — this is exactly the level of detail we need. I pulled together an initial sizing hypothesis (attached) that models two scenarios:

Scenario A (conservative):
- Reserve for sustained baseline + 2x burst headroom
- GPU mix: mix of A100/80G-type reserved slots + a pool of quantized T4-style instances for batch overflow
- Estimated committed GPUs: 28 (serve layer) + 6 (batch) — assumes continuous KV cache hotness for chat sessions

Scenario B (optimistic):
- Reserve baseline only and rely on short-term burst autoscale + routing fallback to slightly larger model variants
- GPU mix: 20 reserved GPUs + 10 burst-capable nodes on demand

A few follow-up asks to refine the model:
- Can you share a short histogram of request inter-arrival times during a burst? That helps determine batching efficiency.
- Do your clients retry aggressively on 5xx? We assume a low retry rate in the hypothesis.

I’m happy to walk through the attached workbook (sizing-hypothesis.xlsx) on a call. Proposed times: Thu 26th 13:00–14:00 PT or Fri 27th 09:00–09:30 PT.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Pre-Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
